candidates.question: How can I tell which jobs need attention before customers complain?
candidates.reason: Strong consequence, cross-industry fit, concrete exception mechanism and immediate visual tension.

candidates.question: How many jobs are waiting for someone to notice?
candidates.reason: Strong hook but less precise as an answer-first buyer question.

candidates.question: Why does every unusual job end up with the owner?
candidates.reason: Commercially relevant but overlaps the unpublished owner-approval package.

candidates.question: Which customer promises exist only in someone’s inbox?
candidates.reason: Useful trust angle but too close to recent inbox and customer-update content.

candidates.question: What breaks when the owner takes Friday off?
candidates.reason: Recognisable but close to existing owner-dependency content.

candidates.question: Why is the team busy while work still waits?
candidates.reason: Broadly relevant but the failing mechanism is less visible.

candidates.question: Why is an accepted quote still not ready to start?
candidates.reason: Below threshold and duplicates recent handover work.

candidates.question: How can a business automate task creation?
candidates.reason: Mechanism-first, narrow, generic and visually weak.
